Facts:
- Imelda Rooke said the compressors were without power for about 9 minutes. (source: Imelda Rooke, plant shift supervisor)
- Imelda Rooke was supervising the afternoon shift in the packing hall when the lights flickered and the compressor noise died away. (source: Imelda Rooke, plant shift supervisor)
- The compressors in the freezer rooms were restarted in sequence after the generator was running again, to avoid a surge. (source: Tobin Marsh, refrigeration technician)
- Rooke ordered the packing hall staff to keep all freezer doors shut once the power failed. (source: Imelda Rooke, plant shift supervisor)
- The temperature logger for Freezer Room 1 recorded a smaller rise than Freezer Room 2 over the same period. (source: Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative temperature logger)
- Aldous Pennick had been moving pallets from the loading dock into Freezer Room 2 shortly before the power loss. (source: Aldous Pennick, forklift driver)
- The generator was a 400 kVA diesel set that the cooperative had serviced in the spring. (source: Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative generator controller log)
- The controller log shows the generator had been carrying the full plant load since 14:30 without any recorded alarm before the stop. (source: Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative generator controller log)
- The standby generator at Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative's Dovecote Processing Plant shut down at 15:42. (source: Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative generator controller log)
- Freezer Room 2 held roughly 18 tonnes of packed mackerel at the time of the shutdown. (source: Tobin Marsh, refrigeration technician)

- The generator controller log recorded the engine stopping at 15:42 and a manual start command being entered at a later time. (source: Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative generator controller log)
- Pennick reported that the freezer room door had been propped open for the pallet moves for several minutes. (source: Aldous Pennick, forklift driver)
- The mains supply to the plant had been disconnected at 14:30 by the utility for planned cable work scheduled to last until 17:00. (source: Imelda Rooke, plant shift supervisor)
- Tobin Marsh said the compressors were without power for about 17 minutes. (source: Tobin Marsh, refrigeration technician)

- The Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative temperature logger showed Freezer Room 2 at minus 21.1 degrees Celsius at its last reading before the compressors were restarted. (source: Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative temperature logger)
- The ambient temperature in the yard was around 34 degrees Celsius that afternoon. (source: Tobin Marsh, refrigeration technician)
- The controller log's operator-entered note attributed the stop solely to the fuel tank running low. (source: Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative generator controller log)

The plant had been relying on the 400 kVA diesel generator since the mains supply was disconnected at 14:30 for planned utility cable work. Temperature loggers indicated a rise in both freezer rooms, with Freezer Room 2 experiencing a larger temperature increase than Freezer Room 1 before the refrigeration units resumed operation.

Sources: Imelda Rooke, plant shift supervisor; Tobin Marsh, refrigeration technician; Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative temperature logger; Aldous Pennick, forklift driver; Greyling Quay Fish Cooperative generator controller log

Facts:
- At about 2:15 p.m. on a Thursday in early October, a drum of floor-stripper concentrate was punctured in the basement supply store of Tovane University Hospital and began leaking onto the concrete floor. (source: Tovane University Hospital Facilities Log)
- No patient areas were affected, and the Safety Office sent no one to the emergency department from the incident. (source: Tovane Hospital Safety Office Incident Report)
- The monitor's alarm threshold is set at 10 parts per million, and it sounded a local horn on the laundry level. (source: Basement Level 2 Vapor Monitor)
- Imogen Harstad noticed a sharp, fishy smell drifting through the linen sorting room shortly before the horn sounded. (source: Imogen Harstad, linen services supervisor)
- The Facilities Log notes that the floor drain in the supply store was plugged with a rubber mat before the spill reached it. (source: Tovane University Hospital Facilities Log)
- The vapor monitor readings fell below 10 parts per million at 3:32 p.m. (source: Basement Level 2 Vapor Monitor)
- The sole cause of the puncture was a forklift fork tine being driven into the drum when the stack was set down. (source: Desmond Okafor, forklift operator)
- Clean linen deliveries to the surgical wing were delayed while the laundry level stayed closed. (source: Imogen Harstad, linen services supervisor)
- The Facilities Log records that the ventilation unit serving the supply store was switched to full exhaust at 2:24 p.m. (source: Tovane University Hospital Facilities Log)
- A two-person hospital spill team in chemical suits began absorbing the liquid with granular pads at 2:41 p.m. (source: Tovane Hospital Safety Office Incident Report)
- The laundry level stayed closed for about 90 minutes before staff were allowed back. (source: Tovane University Hospital Facilities Log)
- The pallet had been delivered that morning by an outside supplier and had not been rewrapped. (source: Tovane Hospital Safety Office Incident Report)
- The leaking drum held an alkaline stripper containing ethanolamine, and about 30 gallons escaped before the drum was upended and sealed. (source: Tovane Hospital Safety Office Incident Report)
- The contaminated absorbent was sealed into six lined containers for removal by a licensed waste contractor. (source: Tovane Hospital Safety Office Incident Report)
- Harstad told her sorting crew to leave through the east stairwell and close the fire door behind them. (source: Imogen Harstad, linen services supervisor)
- Desmond Okafor was moving a pallet of four 55-gallon drums from the loading bay to a storage rack when the incident occurred. (source: Desmond Okafor, forklift operator)
- Desmond Okafor reported that he had driven his forklift for the whole shift without any mechanical problem. (source: Desmond Okafor, forklift operator)
- The Basement Level 2 Vapor Monitor registered an amine reading of 14 parts per million at 2:19 p.m. (source: Basement Level 2 Vapor Monitor)
- The laundry level stayed closed for about 3 hours before staff were allowed back. (source: Imogen Harstad, linen services supervisor)
- The sole cause of the puncture was the protruding pallet board striking the drum as the stack was lifted. (source: Tovane Hospital Safety Office Incident Report)
output:
On a Thursday in early October at about 2:15 p.m., a drum of floor-stripper concentrate was punctured in the basement supply store of the hospital. The incident occurred while a pallet of four 55-gallon drums was being moved from the loading bay to a storage rack. About 30 gallons of the alkaline stripper, which contained ethanolamine, escaped onto the concrete floor before the drum was upended and sealed. The floor drain in the supply store had been plugged with a rubber mat before the spill reached it. A vapor monitor registered an amine reading of 14 parts per million at 2:19 p.m., sounding a local horn on the laundry level. Staff noticed a sharp, fishy smell drifting through the linen sorting room and evacuated through the east stairwell. The ventilation unit serving the supply store was switched to full exhaust at 2:24 p.m., and a two-person hospital spill team began absorbing the liquid with granular pads at 2:41 p.m. The contaminated absorbent was sealed into six lined containers for removal. No patient areas were affected, and no one was sent to the emergency department. The laundry level stayed closed for a period before staff were allowed back, which caused delays to clean linen deliveries to the surgical wing. Vapor monitor readings fell below the alarm threshold at 3:32 p.m.

Sources: Tovane University Hospital Facilities Log, Tovane Hospital Safety Office Incident Report, Basement Level 2 Vapor Monitor, Imogen Harstad, linen services supervisor, Desmond Okafor, forklift operator

An on-call facilities engineer was called to the hospital basement, where he found the main breaker for the Ward 4 lighting and general-outlet panel in the open position. The breaker was open solely because it tripped on an overload surge when the generator took the load, although conflicting records alternatively attributed it to incomplete earlier maintenance. The generator fuel day tank was at 82 percent capacity, and the monthly generator test had last been completed on 2 March. Supply to the hospital's street was restored at 03:52, and the facility returned to mains supply at 04:10. Ward 4 general power was restored after the panel breaker was closed by hand.
